thread:
claire: FYI rolling alert: several us-east-1 GPU warm-pool nodes failed to complete keystore handshakes after midnight firewall tighten. Warm-pool stayed at 0/50 for ~45m.

priya: ugh. can you paste the error lines?

claire: sure, from node logs:
```
2026-03-24T00:12:03Z gpu-node-12 keystore: decrypt err=KMS_DECRYPT_DENIED code=403 attempt=1
2026-03-24T00:12:05Z gpu-node-12 http: POST https://audit-shipper.internal/v1/logs -> 403 Forbidden
```

alex: 403 to audit-shipper usually means egress path not on allowlist. We tightened egress rules yesterday to deny-by-default + allowlist per-controlplane-ip. Looks like the NAT ENI used by warm-pool wasn't included.

priya: Are these ENIs ephemeral per-warmpool allocation? If so we missed automating ENI discovery in the firewall job.

claire: Yes—they're ephemeral. The warm-pool uses a per-subnet ephemeral NAT (aws-managed) so ENI IDs differ on every roll. The controlplane SR sets were updated but worker subnets were left to inherit default-deny.

devops-bot: runbook: create temporary allow rule for warm-pool subnet -> allow [kms.us-east-1.internal, audit-shipper.internal] TTL=3h. Requesting approval.

alex: short term options: (A) add temporary allowlist for the subnet CIDR (fast), (B) detect NAT ENIs and add them to allowlist (safer, narrower), (C) revert the deny policy.

priya: prefer B. We'll script ENI discovery and autopatch the firewall for 3h window. alex: +1. Also add a KMS 5xx alert (threshold 1% over 5m) — we saw throttling risk during retries.

claire: cost impact: autoscaler rebalanced to eu nodes once joins failed, added ~1.9k/day in cross-region egress until mitigation. Need to record in incident cost tracker.

devops-bot: sched:firewall-allow --subnet subnet-warm-east-01 --endpoints kms.us-east-1.internal,audit-shipper.internal --ttl 3h :white_check_mark:

keystore-bot: allowlist:applied subnet=subnet-warm-east-01 by=claire expires=2026-03-24T03:12:00Z ticket=INFRA-7621

priya: Canary: spinning 4 nodes now. watching metric keystore.decrypt.success_rate and warm_pool.fill_time.

alex: Also track kms.decrypt.retry_count and keystore.proxy.latency. If retry_count > 20 for any node -> alert oncall.

priya: Canary results: 4/4 joined, decrypt.success_rate -> 100%, median decrypt.latency 150ms (was 2.1s). Warm_pool.fill_time back to normal.

claire: Good. Next steps: 1) keep temporary allow for 3h and then auto-remove, 2) open RFC to move warm-pool keystore egress through controlplane egress (static ENI or NAT gateway we manage), 3) add firewall CI test that simulates ephemeral ENI churn and validates allowlist generation.

alex: Compliance note: document the exception, approver (infra-owner), TTL and add to audit logs for 180d. Security asked for an explanation of why ephemeral ENIs were missed.

priya: I'll draft the postmortem + runbook and link to RFC. Tagging infra-policy and security for review.

claire: thanks. closing the mitigation once the allow TTL expires and nodes remain stable. I'll paste the postmortem link here when ready. :thumbsup:
